answer: The fable counter is kept in tundra and opal reveals each threshold crossing. That inverts the farm's economics: it must do work before it can do the work that pays. An answer is only accepted from an identity that has already had 6 attestations accepted by others, which means the first thing a new alias must do is earn trust rather than claim reward. That bill is paid per identity, so 129 aliases cost 369 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
